messages:
Anna R: quick sanity check — ran speculative decode on caliban-14b-4q with early-exit gating and a tiny branch sampler, saw ~1.55x median token throughput on p3-like shape, but some weird long-answer drift on summarization sets. anyone else seen that pattern?
Mike L: nice. can you paste the run command + config?
Anna R: sure:
```
# local harness
./run_speculative.sh --model caliban-14b-4q --quant q4_0 --speculative true \\
  --branch-samples 3 --early-exit-thresh 0.82 --cache-warmup 4 --batch 8
```
results: latency P50 down 35%, P95 down 20%, tokens/sec up ~55% overall. QA exact-match stable, but XSum ROUGE-L dropped ~3.2 pts on long summaries.
Sophia Z: what eval protocol? prompt set size, seeds, temp?
Anna R: A/B on the same 1k prompts (500 QA mix, 300 XSum, 200 code doc), 5 seeds, temp=0.7 for gen tasks. Kept sampling deterministic for QA (topk+seed).
Claire T: did you also test with the non-speculative fallback enabled? e.g. if sampler confidence < threshold we reissue normal decode?
Anna R: yes fallback enabled after 5ms stall. fallback rate ~6% overall, but for long XSum examples fallback was 18% and those still produced shorter outputs than baseline.
Mike L: could be kv-cache alignment or quant-induced probability mass shift. caliban's tied-embed quant matrix had some small bias in softmax tail when using q4_0 in our previous runs.
Sophia Z: suggest a quick ablation: run same spec decode with quant q4_1 and with tied-embed dequant trick disabled. compare per-token prob deltas vs baseline.
Anna R: on it. also adding a targeted eval: compute per-token logp diags and prefix perplexity drift across length buckets. if drift correlates with early exits we have a spec+quant interaction.
Claire T: ops-bot FYI can track rollout canary for dedicated and log fallback spikes per-route?
ops-bot: scheduled canary monitor for caliban-14b-4q speculative on route /gen/caliban. alert if fallback_rate > 10% over 5m. :white_check_mark:
Mike L: also include a prompt-sensitivity test: take 50 long-summary prompts and append neutral filler tokens to change tokenization alignment — helps surface tied-embed drift.
Anna R: good idea. I'll run the q4_1 + dequant-off + prompt-shift ablations overnight and post short logs here tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
Sophia Z: if we see consistent ROUGE regressions but stable QA, might add a simple hybrid: use speculative for short/hard prompts, normal decode for long-narrative summarization. quick policy rule in router.
Anna R: noted — I'll export a quick per-route policy recommendation along with the ablation results.
